sample_unit: LLMs evaluated on 4 clinical error-detection test sets
models_evaluated: 15 diverse LLMs (not named in the text)

links.outcome: Pairwise discrimination versus aggregate F1 for LLM clinical error detection across 4 test sets and 3 languages
links.effect: 13 of 15 models fell below random pairwise discrimination despite moderate-looking F1 scores; F1 and pairwise accuracy move in opposite directions under the same bias, so F1 ranking may favor the weakest discriminators.
links.quote: In particular, evaluating 15 diverse LLMs on 4 standardized clinical error-detection test sets across 3 languages, we find that 13 of 15 models fall below the level of random pairwise discrimination, even while achieving F1 scores that standard practice would read as moderate.

unlisted_practices: Paired evaluation of erroneous notes and their clean counterparts in error-detection benchmarks
Scoring the evidence models cite in their outputs to diagnose where discrimination breaks down

screen.reason: Empirically tests and evaluates 15 LLMs across multiple error-detection datasets and languages, specifically demonstrating how evaluation methodology/metric choices (paired evaluations vs standard aggregate metrics) affect safety-critical validation prior to deployment.

primary.practice: paired benchmark evaluation metrics for model validation
